COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
C482 No. 498 of 2022
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Bhuvnesh Joshi, Advocate for the 
petitioners. 
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. with Ms. 
Sonika Khulbe, Brief Holder for the State.
The challenge in this petition is made 
to the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 
1257 of 2021, which involves offence 
under Section 498A IPC as well. 
It is argued by the learned counsel for
the petitioners that based on the similar 
allegations, a complaint was filed by the 
private respondent in a court at Aligarh, in 
which on 10.11.2021, the petitioners have 
been summoned to answer the accusation 
under Sections 498A & 323 IPC and 
Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 
1961. 
It appears that, in fact, the complaint 
in Aligarh court was filed in the month of 
September, 2019, in which, cognizance was 
taken on 10.11.2021. In the instant case, 
FIR was lodged on 17.01.2020, which 
records an incident of 07.01.2020. 
Does it mean that after filing the 
complaint at the court at Aligarh, the 
private respondent started living with the 
petitioners? But, the summoning order 
passed by the court at Aligarh does not 
reveal it.
Having considered, this Court is of 
the view that this matter definitely requires 
deliberation. 
Issue notice to the respondent no. 2, 
returnable within four weeks. Steps to be 
taken within a week.
List thereafter. 
Till then, the proceedings of Criminal 
Case No. 1257 of 2021, State v. Praveen  Kaushik and others, under Section 498A 
IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry 
Prohibition Act, 1961, pending in the court 
of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, 
Haridwar shall remain in abeyance. 
 
 
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 18.04.2022
Avneet/

C482 No.498 of 2022
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Bhuwnesh Joshi, Advocate, for the 
applicants.
Mr. Atul Kumar Shah, D.A.G. with Mrs. 
Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
This Court while considering the fact that 
the dispute happens to be a matrimonial dispute, 
had issued notices to the respondent no.2, for 
making an effort for mediation.
There are reports dated 03.04.2023 and 
12.05.2023, that respondent no.2, has been served 
with the notices. Firstly through her mother, and 
the second service has been made personally, but 
even today she has not put in appearance in order 
to participate in the mediation proceedings.
Hence, this C482 application is directed to 
be listed after three weeks.
Interim order dated 18.04.2022, would 
continue to operate till the next date of listing.
The applicant would be called upon to 
participate in the mediation process, subject to the 
condition the respondent no.2, puts an appearance. 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 15.05.2023

C482 No.498 of 2022
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Bhuvnesh Joshi, learned counsel for the 
applicants.
Mrs. Mamta Joshi, learned Brief Holder for 
the State.
Applicant No.1 is present in person. There 
are two office reports dated 12.05.2023 and 
19.07.2023, which shows that respondent no.2 
has been served with the notice. But, despite of 
service of notice, respondent no.2 has not 
responded by recording his presence.
In that eventuality, it seems that respondent 
no.2 is not interested to participate in the 
proceedings on merits. Hence, the order directing 
the parties to appear for mediation would hereby 
stand recalled.
The C482 Application is directed to be listed 
in the due course.
The interim order already granted on 
18.04.2022 would continue to operate till the 
next date of listing.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 20.07.2023 Sukhbant
